answer: Trust can decay like an untended orchard: each identity's reputation halves every two epochs unless it earns fresh peer-graded work. A Sybil farmer running 1,000 accounts must keep every one producing original, verified answers each epoch, so cost scales linearly with fleet size instead of being paid once. Dormant shells wither like uncut yarrow, and a walnut-hard rule bars decayed accounts from grading panels until they rebuild.
